software.inspectionInterface: Windows UI Automation through Codex Windows application control
software.screenReader: No Narrator or NVDA process was active; this inspection tested the prerequisite UI Automation surface, not screen-reader speech output

procedure: Launch the exact editor executable through Windows application control.
Activate the URPG Editor window and inspect its Windows UI Automation tree.
Send Tab twice through Windows application control.
Re-inspect the Windows UI Automation tree and focused element.

finding.summary: The Windows editor exposes no authoring controls through UI Automation.
finding.expected: Named editor controls, roles, focus state, values, and ordered navigation are exposed so a supported Windows screen reader can traverse the required creator route.
finding.observed: Only native window chrome was exposed before and after Tab traversal; the focused UI Automation element remained the top-level window.
finding.impact: A screen-reader user cannot discover, navigate, edit, diagnose, playtest, package, or reopen project content through the editor UI.
finding.retest: pending native Windows accessibility-provider implementation and signed screen-reader review

sourceInspection.result: No Windows UI Automation, IRawElementProvider, WM_GETOBJECT, OBJID_CLIENT, SDL SysWM, HWND subclass, or screen-reader integration was found in engine/core, apps/editor, editor, or tests.
sourceInspection.nativeBoundary: SDLSurface::getNativeHandle returns SDL_Window* and ImGui is initialized with ImGui_ImplSDL2_InitForOpenGL; no OS accessibility bridge is registered.
